description: The qualification provides comprehensive knowledge and practical skills in mulberry cultivation, integrated farming, and silkworm rearing technology, along with allied areas of sericulture. The curriculum covers mulberry morphology, varieties, and planting systems; soil management, irrigation, mechanization, and integrated farming practices; rearing house establishment, equipment, disinfection, and environmental control; techniques of Chawki and late-age rearing, spinning, cocoon harvesting, and pest and disease management. It further includes farm management and sericulture extension, silkworm seed technology, and reeling/post-cocoon technology, ensuring exposure to the entire sericulture value chain. Students will learn to adopt scientific practices in cultivation and rearing, manage farms effectively, apply improved seed and reeling technologies, and explore opportunities in entrepreneurship, value addition, and government-supported sericulture enterprises.
